turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Priya, Sara with HyperSale. Could I take 30 seconds to explain why I’m calling about reducing new-hire ramp time, then you decide?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: HyperSale lets new hires practise realistic buyer calls before going live, with quote-backed coaching. How long until yours handle calls independently today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: It varies by rep. Ramp time isn’t really the problem I’m trying to solve, though.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Understood. What sales execution problem are you trying to solve right now, and how is it showing up across the team?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I can’t tell which reps are coachable before they miss quota. By the time it shows up in the numbers, it’s usually too late.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: When it’s too late, how many reps are typically already off track, and what does that cost you in missed revenue or manager time?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Two or three a quarter end up leaving, and I think some of that’s preventable. I haven’t put a clean dollar figure on it, but it eats a lot of manager time.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That sounds costly. Roughly how many manager hours does each struggling rep consume, and what evidence would help you spot coachability earlier?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I don’t track the hours cleanly. I need to see whether a rep actually applies feedback from one freight call to the next before the quota numbers make it obvious.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s exactly what HyperSale tracks week to week, with every score tied to the rep’s words. How are managers assessing that today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly ride-alongs and occasional call reviews. We bought Gong for this kind of visibility and nobody used it, so why would this be different?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Fair concern. Gong reviewed live calls; HyperSale creates repeatable freight practice and shows whether feedback changed the next attempt. What kept managers from using Gong?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly time. Managers saw it as another dashboard to dig through after a full day, so it never became part of their routine.
